definition: Mechanisms that allow an AI agent to store and later retrieve information across interactions, extending beyond what fits in a single context window.
details: Agent memory systems can include short-term working memory (within a session) and long-term memory (persisted across sessions), often implemented using external storage combined with retrieval mechanisms.
story: Picture hiring a brilliant new assistant on their first morning — smart, motivated, but with no idea how anything in your office actually works. In plain words: Mechanisms that allow an AI agent to store and later retrieve information across interactions, extending beyond what fits in a single context window. Here is how it actually plays out: Agent memory systems can include short-term working memory (within a session) and long-term memory (persisted across sessions), often implemented using external storage combined with retrieval mechanisms. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Memory (in AI agents).
